text.p: Spanish energy group Repsol SA will be fully privatised when the state sells its remaining 10.0 percent stake in a share offer which ends on April 25.
A snapshot of the company follows:
(1996 figures are provisional. All figures in pesetas)
WHAT: Repsol is involved in the exploration, production, refining and marketing of crude oil, petroleum products, petrochemicals, liquefied petroleum gases and natural gas.
OPERATING INCOME: 2.77 trillion pesetas versus 2.54 trillion in 1995
NET PROFIT: 119.22 billion pesetas versus 117.72 billion
MARKET CAPITALISATION: 1.8 trillion (share price at 6,000 ptas)
SHARE OFFER: Up to 10.001 percent of capital or 30,002,859 shares. Of these, 4,500,429 will be offered to Repsol employees, making the public offering 25,502,427 shares.

EXECUTIVE BOARD: Executive chairman Alfonso Cortina. Directors: strategic planning - Miguel Angel Remon; financial - Carmelo de las Morenas; external relations - Jorge Segrelles; exploration, chemicals - Antonio Gonzalez-Adalid; refining, marketing - Juan Sancho Rof. Emilio Ybarra, chairman of Banco Bilbao Vizcaya also has a place on Repsol's board.
AREAS OF BUSINESS: Energy, chiefly oil and gas. Has a 45.3 percent stake in Spain's Gas Natural.

INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS: Main interests are a 47.5 percent stake in Astra and an indirect 45 percent stake in Pluspetrol Energy, both in Argentina. Repsol also leads a consortium which bought 60 percent of Peru's La Pampilla refinery. Repsol has a 60 percent stake in Peru's Lima Gas ($9million), and 60 percent of Peru's Solgas ($39million). It also undertakes exploration and production activities in Egypt, the North Sea, and Indonesia.

ALLIANCES: Has energy agreement with Gas Natural and Iberdrola for development of electricity co-generation using natural gas or refinery residues in Spain, as well as cooperation on overseas projects.
HISTORY: Repsol was founded in 1987 on the grouping of state participations in the petrol and gas sectors.
